rules_text:
Rules summary Cheez-Tricks is a trick-taking game where you should avoid some missions (or try to get them all for more points). Deck composition: 2 players: 1-7 3 players: 1-9 4 and 5 players: 1-10 All the cards are dealt, except in 2 players where 20 cards are dealt and 8 are removed from the game. Playing the game: Regular rules for trick-taking game: must follow suit, trump (random on the first round, chose by the player who has the least score on all the others). Highest card of the trump takes the trick; in case of no trumps, highest card of the lead suit takes the trick. Scoring: Number of tricks x 2 if you have not been captured by any cat. Number of tricks x 1 if you have been captured by 1 cat. Zero points if you have been captured by 2 cats. Number of tricks x 3 if you have been captured by all cats. BGA deck by color / cheese: Orange = Parmesan Red = Swiss Green = Roquefort Blue = Brie After rounds = number of players, the player who has the most points is the winner. The Cats: Black Cat: Capture the player who wins a certain trick. Siamese Cat: Capture the player who wins a certain card. White Cat: Capture the first player who wins a certain amount of tricks Gray Cat: Capture the player that wins the most of a card/suit/tricks by the end of the round. Orange Cat: Capture the player that wins the least of a card/suit/tricks by the end of the round. Tuxedo Cat: Capture the player that wins exactly a certain amount of tricks by the end of the round.

[Rating: 6/10] Torselli bga. The hook is that each round has three randomly chosen special "lose" conditions-- e.g. don't catch 3rd trick, or don't catch 3 of blue cheese suit, or don't take 4 tricks in total etc. Each time you fulfill those you earn that Cat. You score your tricks won, but avoid special condition ("cats")-- unless you can catch all three.  Scoring very elegant: no cats you score 2x your tricks; 1 cat your score 1x your tricks; 3 cats you score 4x your tricks. That last bit is the tension that drives the game, and it's coolest feature.
